program: School-based WOW and BAM counseling, education and family support

what: Youth Guidance places counselors and mentors in schools to support young people facing trauma and other barriers to success.
WOW provides group-based support for girls, while BAM helps young men reflect on decisions and strengthen school engagement.
Family assistance and community programs complement this work by addressing immediate needs and connecting students with supportive adults.
strengths: WOW has randomized evidence for reduced depression and post-traumatic stress symptoms, with a transparent utility model.
BAM has multiple randomized studies and a measured early graduation contrast, alongside important scaling cautions.
Current local program counts, direct family cash assistance and original audited costs provide concrete implementation anchors.
reservations: Annual reach is not verified completed trial-equivalent care or unique households; sibling and cash-recipient overlap is unknown.
BAM graduation-to-net-resources and current transfer remain judgments, not measured earnings.
The whole annual denominator covers national and unpriced programs; school resources, public funding replacement and marginal capacity remain uncertain.

sections.what: Youth Guidance, EIN 36-2167032, provides school-based counseling, mentoring, career readiness and family support. Its official giving page identifies the legal recipient and links national and regional routes, including Chicago; no transaction or donor restriction was tested. WOW serves girls in grades 6–12, while BAM works with young men in grades 6–12 across Chicagoland, including Waukegan and the south suburbs. Geographic reach is not precise beneficiary residence within the pinned metro.
sections.monitoring: The FY2025 annual report gives national WOW reach 4,331 and BAM reach 8,679. Its Illinois pages report WOW 3,649 and BAM 7,243 participants, not unique completed trial-equivalent courses or households. Community Connections assisted more than 400 families with approximately $150,000 direct cash. The 400 figure includes broader crisis assistance; it does not establish 400 paid recipients. The reference assumes 400 equally paid household units, with concentrated 100/20-recipient Jensen sensitivities at the same aggregate cash. Current symptom-improvement and satisfaction percentages are noncausal monitoring, not fresh randomized effects. Obtain attendance, counselor dose, retention, unique household IDs, grade mix, actual cash allocations and residence.
sections.qualitative:
The original WOW randomized evaluation maps depression and PTSD scales to literature utilities, taking each student's minimum condition utility rather than adding comorbid gains. Anxiety is omitted from its cost-utility model. Table 5 assumes a full year of benefit and estimates $58,025/QALY for combined depression/PTSD. The study's $2,300 actual-participant cost is converted using .6525 uptake for its ITT analysis. Recovering 2,300/58,025=.039638 participant-equivalent utility therefore does NOT require applying uptake again. This is modeled utility, not directly measured local clinical QALYs. Current transfer .5 reflects grade mix, dose, counselors and population; half a year is a finite duration judgment, with quarter-year onset and 3% discount. No lifetime protection, arrest-to-injury conversion or extra mortality credit is added.

For BAM, original first-trial Table VI reports on-time graduation ITT .0297 and participant IV .0714, both p<.10, n=2,740. These are probability differences, not 19 percentage points: the headline 19% is relative. Later scaling trials did not detect significant outcomes in new populations. Pooled school engagement projected up to five graduation points is not observed pooled diploma completion or earnings. The reference uses .0714 participant IV with .25 current transfer, explicitly weak across current grades/dose/settings. It is not automatically applied as current causal graduation. WOW's study did not establish academic gains. BAM violence, other counseling, afterschool, career and national income effects remain unpriced and unknown, including harms.
sections.cost:
FY2025 audited expense $54,652,685 plus $204,922 direct event benefits netted against revenue gives full gross recognized resources $54,857,607. Recorded donated services and in-kind inputs are already included; no duplicate addback. FY2024 uses $56,011,499 + $276,981 = $56,288,480; FY2023 $46,884,765 + $195,100 = $47,079,865. Comparable mean is $52,741,984. These are whole national-recipient resources, not a Chicago-only or WOW-only budget. Unrecognized school space/staff and partner opportunity costs are unknown, not free; K=0 is only a recognized-boundary reference, with 25%-of-C additional budget stress and full unknown. The original FY2025 audit opinion is dated December 10, 2025; publication date is not inferred.

b=.5 denotes a conditional annual funded-work response beyond replacement funding, school capacity and counselor constraints, not a second donor haircut on measured incremental outcomes. Full annual cost stays in the denominator; b=1 is separate. WOW local 3,649 × .5 funding × .039638 utility × .5 transfer × .5 years × .95 residence, discounted after .25-year onset, yields 17.049469 clinical QALYs. The initial undiscounted conditional health-only price is preserved. All-population clinical fields retain national WOW reach; they are health-only, not complete national welfare.

BAM local 7,243 × .5 funding gives 3,621.5 exposed participant units. Judged current graduation probability .0714 × .25 gives 64.643775 additional-graduate hypotheses. A separate unsupported $1,000 net annual household-resource gain lasts only three years after four years' delay. It must be net of taxes, benefit withdrawal, commuting, childcare, college/training opportunity costs, displaced earnings and other employment; no gross salary or lifetime diploma premium is treated as observed. Positive BAM resource overlap defaults 1 because no BAM health is priced centrally; half-overlap is shown, and negative earnings or graduation changes are retained fully. This is not ordinary survivor earnings.

Current direct cash gives an additional resource anchor, not a social-income claim. $150,000 divided among judged 400 paid households, .5 additional versus other assistance and .9 net usable resources gives $168.75 per recipient. Positive WOW overlap .5 and full incremental family-process burden $20 give $64.375 net. Other WOW families lose $20, and BAM families lose $20. These burden priors concern actual incremental usable household resources versus alternatives, not retail counseling prices or monetized ordinary school hours. Cash gains and signed benefit withdrawal are netted with burden BEFORE one log. Household baseline is judged $30,000/year; future graduate baseline is $20,000/year. One welfare-equivalent person per household is explicit; family members are not automatically added.

Central WOW and BAM households are assumed disjoint, although students may be siblings. Joint-family cases combine both $20 burdens in a single household-year log. Cash recipients are assumed a subset of WOW-only households, not separate welfare people; this allocation is unverified. Two-participants-per-household aggregation preserves both participants' full costs and earning gains before the joint log, assuming similarly situated co-resident participants. Current burden/cash year and delayed earnings years 4–6 are distinct time slices, so future resource logs do not double count same-year resources. Full health harms cover the distinct WOW+BAM individual union even when households overlap.

The production .5 × households × discounted years × log(1 + joint net/baseline) bridge gives 2.419906 signed resource equivalents, combining with health to 19.469375, or $28.176358 million per ten combined equivalents, not ten clinical QALYs. Clinical-null keeps cash, earnings hypotheses and all burdens. No cash additionality, no earnings, no graduation, zero-expansion, true-zero, unknown and adverse controls differ. Complete portfolio and world-net effects remain unknown, not zero or a lower bound.

The cash transfer is already an expense in C: do not add it to resource cost again or charge the same donating households twice. Counterparty stress represents a separate displaced-beneficiary/public-budget alternative from incremental assistance, not the donor cost already in C. It allocates full pre-overlap additional cash to distinct households, with low-baseline fixed-budget displacement separate. Outside school/provider own-resource stress excludes staff/input costs already priced in C or K. Central payer incidence is unknown-neutral, not observed zero. No complete global-benefit claim follows from recipient cash gains.
sections.funding: FY2025 audit reports government grants $28,749,724, revenue $46,408,813 and an $8,243,872 net-asset decline. Net assets total $40,156,046, but $19,197,138 is donor restricted and $17,003,852 board designated; $5,273,375 financial assets are available for general expenditure within one year. $800,000 was drawn against the $10 million callable line of credit. These figures indicate funding and cash-flow constraints but do not establish a priced marginal expansion. The current Bright Futures campaign seeks a $30 million impact fund and $50 million endowment; campaign scale is not immediate clinical capacity. Existing school counseling, mentoring, public contracts and other family assistance are relevant alternatives. Ask for a funded counselor/caseload tranche, its grade/dose/Chicago share, substitution, school resource costs and cash targeting. No next-gift price or complete annual portfolio EV is verified.

historicalAlphaModel.costScope: Full Youth Guidance national audited FY25 expenses plus direct special-event benefits; recognized resources included. K adds unknown unrecognized resources. No restriction to WOW or Chicago costs.
historicalAlphaModel.geographicAttribution: Only local WOW reach L=3649 times g=.95 judgment, not national N=4331 times a headquarters share. Chicago and Waukegan anchors intersect the 13-county MSA; exact residence pending.
historicalAlphaModel.formula: Q_all=b*(N*q*t*D+H); Q_MSA=b*(L*g*q*t*D+Hlocal); cost=C+K; price per 10 QALYs=10*cost/Q_MSA only when Q_MSA>0.
historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: Original trial: usual school/community electives and services. Current scenario discounts transfer and allows zero resource response if a gift replaces grants/reserves; no assumption that participants otherwise receive nothing.
historicalAlphaModel.attribution: Whole-recipient ordinary gift; national costs retained; only MSA health counted. Other portfolio treated as unknown signed health, not asserted valueless. q preserves economic-study participant denominator.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: Utility mapping, effect persistence, current counselor/age/dose comparability, survey response, duplicate reach, finance elasticity, residence and other portfolio can dominate. Scenarios are not confidence intervals.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeOutcomes: WOW randomized symptom scales and mapped combined depression/PTSD utility; annual reach; recipient audited expenses. BAM arrests/education not converted to health.

inputs.name: q
inputs.unit: trial-model utility gain per participant-equivalent year
inputs.rationale: Reconstruct 2300/58025=0.039638 from original Table 5's combined depression/PTSD ICER and cost per actual participant. inputs.rationale: Discount for grades 6–12 vs original high-school sample, intensity/completion, staff qualifications, survey mapping and current counterfactual. Does not reapply the trial's 65% offer take-up; q already uses a participant-equivalent denominator.

inputs.name: D
inputs.unit: years of utility benefit per annual participant reach
inputs.rationale: Half-year benefit then zero. No lifetime protection or two-year accumulation; same participant across fiscal years must not receive duplicate long-term benefit.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Hypothetical half response relative to historic service mix. Reserves, restrictions, contracted revenue and staffing can make this zero. No verified incremental tranche.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: MSA residence share of local-reach benefits
inputs.rationale: Chicago and Waukegan are local anchors; Chicagoland is not a precise 13-county residence boundary. This is not 95% of national output.

inputs.name: K
inputs.unit: USD unrecognized net partner resource costs
inputs.rationale: Conditionally zero, stress-tested at 25% of C; school space/staff and unpaid resources not priced. Recorded donated resources are not added twice.

inputs.unit: signed annual non-WOW national QALYs before funding response
inputs.rationale: Conditionally zero. BAM and other work can benefit or harm; arrest reductions and earnings cannot be directly relabeled QALYs.

inputs.name: Hlocal

inputs.rationale: Conditionally zero, separate from national health; ±50 cases are judgments with overlap deducted in future work.
